item.text:
**6B.6 Research Note: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi in 2024**

Verdict: mixed, leaning partially yes. I found real evidence of targeted relief, service-system adjustments, and some crisis de-escalation, but also strong evidence that major suffering continued to be handled through exclusion, rushed policy, and repression rather than consistently humane correction.

**Accepted claims**

- **Arab Republic of Egypt: Technical Assistance Report - Public Investment Management Assessment** — IMF — 2024-04-02 — https://www.imf.org/en/publications/technical-assistance-reports/issues/2024/04/02/arab-republic-of-egypt-technical-assistance-report-public-investment-management-assessment-547051  
  Egypt had already taken steps to improve infrastructure access and public investment management through new legislation, new information systems, and staff-capacity work; the report also ties this to Education 2.0 and health-infrastructure rollout. This is evidence of technocratic correction during stress, not just rhetoric.  
  QIDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.5`, `6B.2`

- **Promoting Inclusive Human Capital Development and Building Resilience in Egypt through Cash Transfer Programs** — World Bank — 2024-05-28 — https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2024/05/28/promoting-inclusive-human-capital-development-and-building-resilience-in-egypt-through-cash-transfer-programs  
  Takaful and Karama is described as targeted, conditional, and institutionally managed, with proxy means testing, a grievance mechanism, and a dynamic social registry. That is strong evidence of active mitigation of inflation and poverty shocks.  
  QIDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Arab Republic of Egypt: Third Review Under the Extended Arrangement Under the Extended Fund Facility** — IMF — 2024-07-29 — https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/29/pr24293-egypt-imf-exec-board-completes-3rd-rev-extended-arr-eff  
  The IMF says inflation was easing, FX shortages had been eliminated, fiscal targets were met, and social spending was supposed to be protected. This supports a limited claim that the shock response was beginning to stabilize conditions for households.  
  QIDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.5`

- **New World Bank US$700 million Support to Help Egypt Achieve More Sustainable, Diversified and Resilient Growth** — World Bank Group — 2024-06-24 — https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/24/new-world-bank-us-700-million-support-to-help-egypt-achieve-more-sustainable-diversified-and-resilient-growth  
  The reform package included water and sanitation sustainability, electricity-loss reduction, renewables, and stronger SOE governance. That is relevant because it shows service-capacity and resilience investment during a hard year.  
  QIDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.5`

- **Launch of the Joint UN Programme under the Joint Platform for Migrants and Refugees in Egypt** — UNHCR Egypt — 2024-09-30 — https://www.unhcr.org/eg/news/launch-joint-un-programme-under-joint-platform-migrants-and-refugees-egypt  
  Egypt, the UN, and the EU launched a program to support health and education for refugees and migrants in vulnerable situations after the Sudan influx. This is the clearest positive crisis-displacement evidence I found.  
  QIDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Egypt co-led Gaza ceasefire / bridging proposal** — Presidency of the Republic of Egypt — 2024-08-16 — https://www.presidency.eg/en/%D9%82%D8%B3%D9%85_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9/news1682024/  
  Egypt co-led a ceasefire bridging proposal tied to UNSC 2735 and humanitarian provisions. That is direct evidence of crisis de-escalation aimed at reducing civilian harm in a major displacement emergency.  
  QIDs: `6B.6`

**Contrary claims**

- **Egypt: New law threatens to reduce access to healthcare for millions** — Amnesty International — 2024-07-30 — https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-new-law-threatens-to-reduce-access-to-healthcare-for-millions/  
  Sisi ratified Law 87 of 2024, which privatized management of public health facilities without price regulation and was adopted without adequate consultation. This is strong evidence against crisis-sensitive, access-preserving service stewardship.  
  QIDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.5`

- **Egypt: Education Restricted for Refugees** — Human Rights Watch — 2024-12-02 — https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/egypt-education-restricted-for-refugees  
  Tens of thousands of refugee and asylum-seeking children were kept out of school because of residency requirements, fees, discrimination, and limited free public education. This is direct evidence of avoidable suffering persisting for a displacement-affected group.  
  QIDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Egypt Authorities Must End Campaign of Mass Arrests and Forced Returns of Sudanese Refugees** — Amnesty International — 2024-06-19 — https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/egypt-authorities-must-end-campaign-of-mass-arrests-and-forced-returns-of-sudanese-refugees/  
  Border Guard Forces and police mass-arrested Sudanese refugees, held women, men, and children in cruel conditions, and forced returns without asylum access. This is strong negative evidence on avoiding suffering during conflict displacement.  
  QIDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.3`, `6B.2`

- **Egypt: Halt crackdown on people voicing concerns over economic crisis** — Amnesty International — 2024-05-13 — https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/  
  Authorities arrested protesters, striking workers, and online critics over economic discontent, and did not properly investigate abuse complaints. That weakens any claim that the regime used feedback and correction to reduce suffering from the economic shock.  
  QIDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.5`

- **Egypt: President al-Sisi must reject new asylum law which violates refugee rights** — Amnesty International — 2024-12-03 — https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/12/egypt-president-al-sisi-must-reject-new-asylum-law-which-violates-refugee-rights/  
  Amnesty said the asylum law lacked due process, restricted rights, and failed to protect education, housing, and social security for refugees and asylum seekers. This cuts against a transparent, protection-oriented response to displacement.  
  QIDs: `6B.6`, also `6B.2`, `6B.3`

**Search gap**

- I did not find strong independent evidence of a national crisis-response dashboard, public after-action review process, or routine publication of outcome metrics showing how Sisi measured and reduced suffering across crises in 2024.
- The strongest positives are program-specific and often filtered through IMF, World Bank, or UN partnership reporting rather than a transparent Egyptian government monitoring system.
